prompt: Right after two INSERTs, `ls` of the table's directory on `c1` printed nothing. Where were the rows?

choices.text: Nowhere yet: an INSERT is applied at the next compaction
choices.why: The rows were readable at once; compaction merges files that already exist.

choices.text: On c2 and c3 only, since c1 was the coordinator
choices.why: With three copies, c1 is a replica too.

choices.text: In the memtable and the commit log
choices.why: Right. nodetool flush wrote them out as nb-1.

choices.text: In a hidden SSTable that ls does not list
choices.why: SSTables are ordinary files; the directory was empty until the flush.

prompt: An `UPDATE` changed Ana's `CB-012` from 2 to 3 after `nb-1` was flushed. What happened to `nb-1`?

choices.text: It was rewritten in place with the value 3
choices.why: SSTables are never changed once written.

choices.text: Nothing; it went to a newer SSTable
choices.why: Right: quantity 2 in nb-1, quantity 3 in nb-3, until compaction merged them.

choices.text: It was deleted and replaced by nb-3
choices.why: nb-1 stayed until compaction; there were three SSTables.

choices.text: It was marked read-only and moved aside
choices.why: Every SSTable is read-only; nothing moved.

choices.text: Assume UCS, since Cassandra 5.0 introduced it
choices.why: The lab's table got STCS on 5.0.9; UCS is the default only in cassandra_latest.yaml.

choices.text: Look at the default_compaction line of cassandra_latest.yaml
choices.why: That file is the recommended settings, not necessarily the ones in use.

choices.text: Count the SSTables in the data directory
choices.why: The count depends on timing and load, not only on the strategy.

choices.text: Read the compaction line of DESCRIBE TABLE
choices.why: Right. It said SizeTieredCompactionStrategy.

prompt: What did `sstabledump` show in `nb-5`, the SSTable flushed after the `DELETE`?

choices.text: The keyboard row with quantity 1 and a deleted flag on it
choices.why: The old row stayed in nb-4; nb-5 has no cells at all.

choices.text: A row with no cells and a deletion_info timestamp
choices.why: Right: that is the tombstone, the whole of it.

choices.text: An empty file, since a delete removes data
choices.why: A delete adds a marker; it removes nothing.

choices.text: Ana's whole partition, rewritten without the keyboard
choices.why: Nothing is rewritten until compaction.

prompt: The outbox query returned one row, yet the trace reported `Read 1 live rows and 1499 tombstone cells`. What is the lesson's diagnosis?

choices.text: Its deletes pile up, and each read steps over them
choices.why: Right. Each poll pays for every handled item until compaction can drop the tombstones.

choices.text: The deletes failed and the rows are still live
choices.why: They are counted as tombstones, not live rows.

choices.text: The trace counts each row twice, so the real number is half
choices.why: 1499 rows were deleted, and 1499 tombstones were read.

choices.text: The table needs an SAI index on id
choices.why: An index does not remove the tombstones the partition read steps over.

prompt: Above how many tombstones in one read does a Cassandra 5.0.9 node abort the query with an error, by default?
A worker drains a queue partition by deleting each item it handles. Which change does the lesson suggest?

choices.text: Delete faster, so the tombstones are compacted sooner
choices.why: Tombstones stay at least gc_grace_seconds however fast they are written.

choices.text: Raise tombstone_warn_threshold, so that the warnings stop appearing in the log
choices.why: That hides the cost without removing it.

choices.text: Add a time bucket to the key, or store how far the consumer got
choices.why: Right. Either way reads stop walking over handled items.

choices.text: Run nodetool compact every hour on the queue table
choices.why: Compaction keeps tombstones younger than gc_grace_seconds.

prompt: Since an SSTable never changes, a DELETE writes a marker called a ___.
What does `gc_grace_seconds = 864000` mean for a table?

choices.text: Tombstones are kept at least ten days before compaction drops them
choices.why: Right: 864000 seconds is ten days of grace.

choices.text: Rows written to the table expire ten days after they were written
choices.why: That would be a TTL; gc_grace_seconds concerns tombstones.

choices.text: Repair runs automatically on every node of the cluster every ten days
choices.why: Nothing runs repair for you; the setting is the deadline you must meet.

choices.text: A deleted row can be undone by the operator for ten days afterwards
choices.why: There is no undo; the tombstone wins over the older row.

prompt: A team lowers `gc_grace_seconds` from ten days to two to reduce tombstones. Their repairs finish once a week. What have they done?

choices.text: Slowed every write, because tombstones are checked more often
choices.why: The setting changes nothing about writes.

choices.text: Nothing harmful, because hinted handoff carries every delete
choices.why: Hints are best effort and expire after max_hint_window.

choices.text: Made repair unnecessary, since tombstones vanish sooner
choices.why: Repair is what carries the tombstone before it vanishes.

choices.text: Made deleted rows able to come back, since a tombstone now goes before repair reaches it
choices.why: Right. The repair deadline shrank to two days and the repairs did not.

prompt: Put the life of a tombstone in order, on a node that saw the delete.
items: The DELETE writes the tombstone to the memtable
A flush writes it to a new SSTable
Compactions copy it forward while it is younger than gc_grace_seconds
A compaction after gc_grace_seconds drops it with the data it shadowed

prompt: Which of these can carry a missed delete to a replica that was down? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Hinted handoff, if the node was down less than max_hint_window
choices.why: Right, best effort.

choices.text: Read repair, if a read compares that replica with another
choices.why: Right, only for rows that are read.

choices.text: nodetool repair
choices.why: Right, and the only one that visits every partition.

choices.text: Compaction on the node that saw the delete
choices.why: Compaction is local; it sends nothing to other nodes.

choices.text: A larger gc_grace_seconds alone
choices.why: It keeps the tombstone longer, but something still has to carry it.

prompt: A node has been down for three weeks, with the default `gc_grace_seconds`. What does the lesson say to do with it?

choices.text: Wipe it and let it rejoin as a new node
choices.why: Right. Its data may hold deletes everyone else has forgotten.

choices.text: Start it and read everything at ALL first
choices.why: A read at ALL read-repairs the same old rows into the others.

choices.text: Start it and run repair at once
choices.why: Repair would spread its rows whose tombstones the others already purged.

choices.text: Raise gc_grace_seconds before starting it
choices.why: The tombstones are already gone; raising it now brings nothing back.

choices.text: The replication factor to 1, and consistency to ONE

choices.text: The compaction strategy to UCS, and the heap to 256 MB

choices.text: A 60-second gc_grace_seconds, and hints switched off

prompt: After the purge, a read at `ONE` from `c1` showed one item. Then `nodetool repair` ran and the deleted item was back. Why did repair copy it?

choices.text: Repair prefers the node that was down most recently
choices.why: Repair has no such preference; it reconciles by timestamp.

choices.text: Repair ignores deletes by design
choices.why: Repair copies tombstones like any data, while they exist.

choices.text: c3 had a row the others lacked, and no tombstone was left to say it was deleted
choices.why: Right. Without the tombstone the old row is simply the newest thing anyone has.

choices.text: The DELETE had failed on c1 and c2
choices.why: It succeeded at QUORUM, and the dumps showed its effect.

prompt: Repair has been failing silently every night for two weeks on a cluster with default settings, and nobody deleted anything unusual. What is at risk?

choices.text: Nothing, since no node was down
choices.why: A missed write needs no outage: a dropped mutation under load leaves a replica behind too.

choices.text: Only performance, since compaction falls behind on the busy nodes
choices.why: Compaction runs independently of repair.

choices.text: The tombstone_failure_threshold will be reached
choices.why: That depends on deletes per partition, not on repair.

choices.text: A missed delete returning, as two weeks exceed the grace
choices.why: Right. Two weeks is past ten days; the guarantee is gone.
